ofi.feature: x_t = OFI summed over (t - h, t]; y_t = mid(t + h) - mid(t) in ticks, mid at the last snapshot with ts <= t + h
ofi.missing_level_convention: missing level (px = 0, sz = 0) takes the worst price of its side before the comparison: 0 for a bid, INT_MAX for an ask
ofi.statement: R^2 measures the fit of future mid change on OFI only; no trading or profit claim is made

breakdown.measured_in: overlapped pass: CUDA events recorded on each stream around every chunk's H2D, kernel and D2H, summed per stage, median over the passes

pipeline.consequence: Transfers dominate: the host-to-device and device-to-host copies are 94% of the pipeline's GPU time (H2D 9.0 ms at 11.7 GB/s, kernel 0.6 ms, D2H 0.4 ms). Overlapping three streams can only hide the kernel and the copy-back behind the input copy, which saved 7.5% of the serial wall time. The design consequence is that the archive should be copied to the card once and stay resident, with every analysis run in that one residency instead of streaming the data per analysis.
pipeline.layout: chunk-major pinned copy built once: chunk i = snapshots [i*n/K, (i+1)*n/K); one contiguous 256-byte-aligned block per chunk holding bid_px, bid_sz, ask_px, ask_sz (each level-major inside the chunk), so every chunk is one cudaMemcpyAsync in and one out

precision.exact_reference: python int over float32 mantissas in the base unit 2**min(exponent) (bench/ref_scans.py), rounded to float64 once
precision.input: float32(px_ticks) * size for every best bid, then every best ask
precision.rationale: Window sums of 100 values over 200,000 top-of-book notionals: float32 naive reaches a maximum relative error of 4.62e-04 because two large prefixes cancel; float64 keeps the maximum at 0.00e+00, inside the 9.1e-09 budget (a tenth of a tick at 11,000,307 ticks), and is the fastest variant that does (float64 qualify), at -6.5% time versus float32 naive.
